subject: Physics
topic: Work, Energy & Power: Conservative Fields & Potential Wells
title: Core 1A Physics Blueprint: Work, Energy & Power Conceptual Ontology
source_authority: Owner WEP Specification & Golden Benchmark Parity

canonical_strategy.stage_1_choose: Demarcate closed system boundary; identify all conservative, non-conservative, and external forces.
canonical_strategy.stage_2_represent: Establish coordinate axes and potential energy datum U = 0; sketch force-displacement or potential well curve.
canonical_strategy.stage_3_connect: Apply Work-Energy Theorem (W_net = Delta K) or Mechanical Energy Conservation (Delta E_mech = W_nc).
canonical_strategy.stage_4_execute_and_check: Execute algebraic integration or balance equations; verify SI dimensions [M][L]^2[T]^-2 and boundary limits.

structural_pillars.name: Work-Kinetic Energy Theorem
structural_pillars.statement: The net scalar work performed by all external, internal, conservative, and non-conservative forces acting on a body equals the exact change in its translational kinetic energy.
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Holds universally in all Newtonian inertial frames for constant or spatially varying forces.

structural_pillars.name: Conservative Vector Fields & Path Independence
structural_pillars.statement: A force field is conservative if and only if its circulation around every closed path vanishes identically, guaranteeing that work between two spatial points depends strictly on endpoints, independent of trajectory.
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Applies to static gravitational, ideal Hookean elastic, and electrostatic fields; fails for dissipative friction or velocity-dependent drag.

structural_pillars.name: Total Mechanical Energy Conservation in Isolated Systems
structural_pillars.statement: In any isolated physical system where non-conservative work vanishes, the sum of total kinetic and potential energy remains strictly invariant throughout the evolution of the system.
structural_pillars.mathematical_invariant: W_{\text{nc}} = 0 \implies E_{\text{mech}} = K + U = \text{const} \implies K_i + U_i = K_f + U_f
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Closed conservative physical systems with zero dissipation at the boundary.

structural_pillars.name: Non-Conservative Dissipation & Thermal Degradation
structural_pillars.statement: Non-conservative forces (such as kinetic friction and viscous drag) alter the total mechanical energy of a system, irreversibly converting organized kinetic/potential energy into microscopic internal thermal energy.
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Systems undergoing dry sliding contact friction, aerodynamic fluid drag, or inelastic collisions.

structural_pillars.name: Instantaneous vs Average Power & Velocity Scaling
structural_pillars.statement: Power is the temporal rate of energy transfer. Instantaneous mechanical power equals the scalar dot product of driving force and instantaneous velocity, producing characteristic high-order power-velocity scaling laws.
structural_pillars.mathematical_invariant: P = \frac{dW}{dt} = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{v}, \quad \bar{P} = \frac{\Delta W}{\Delta t}, \quad F_{\text{drag}} \propto v^2 \implies P \propto v^3
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Continuous mechanical power transmission; engines, hoists, pumps, and aerodynamic resistance.

WEP-01.title: Definition of Mechanical Work & Dot Product
WEP-01.definition: Work is defined as the scalar line integral of vector force along the spatial path of displacement: W = integral F . dr = F s cos theta.
canonical_rules: Only force components collinear with instantaneous displacement do work: dW = F_parallel ds.
Forces perpendicular to instantaneous velocity (such as centripetal tension or frictionless normal reaction on fixed rails) do identically zero work: theta = 90 deg => W = 0.
Work is a coordinate-invariant scalar quantity measured in Joules (1 J = 1 N m = 1 kg m^2 s^-2).
operational_heuristics: Identify the angle theta between force vector and displacement vector.
If force is constant: W = F s cos theta.
If force is perpendicular to velocity at all points: immediately set W = 0.
boundary_conditions: theta = 0 deg: maximum positive work W = +F s.
theta = 90 deg: zero work W = 0.
theta = 180 deg: maximum negative work W = -F s.

WEP-02.title: Work by Variable Forces & Spring Integration
WEP-02.definition: When force varies continuously with position F(x), work equals the definite integral of force with respect to position, corresponding geometrically to the signed area under the F(x) curve.
canonical_rules: For 1D variable force: W = int_{x_i}^{x_f} F(x) dx.
Geometric area above x-axis represents positive work; area below x-axis represents negative work.
For ideal Hookean spring (F_s = -k x), work done by external agent stretching from 0 to x is W_ext = int_0^x k x' dx' = 0.5 k x^2.
operational_heuristics: Sketch the F-x graph; partition into recognizable geometric shapes (rectangles, triangles, trapezoids).
For polynomial forces, evaluate analytical definite integrals [int a x^n dx = a x^(n+1)/(n+1)].
boundary_conditions: Linear spring from relaxation: W = 0.5 k x^2.
Spring stretch between x_1 and x_2: W = 0.5 k (x_2^2 - x_1^2).

WEP-03.title: Work-Energy Theorem & Scalar Invariance
WEP-03.definition: The total work performed on a particle by the vector resultant of all forces acting upon it equals the net change in its kinetic energy: W_net = Delta K = 0.5 m v_f^2 - 0.5 m v_i^2.
canonical_rules: W_net includes all forces without exception: conservative, non-conservative, normal, and applied.
Kinetic energy is quadratic in velocity: K = 0.5 m v^2 = p^2 / (2m).
Stopping distance under constant braking friction scales quadratically with initial speed: s_stop = v_0^2 / (2 mu g).
operational_heuristics: Identify initial and final states; equate algebraic sum of work terms to K_f - K_i.
Eliminates the need for time-dependent kinematic integration when trajectory time is neither given nor sought.
boundary_conditions: v_f = v_i: net work W_net = 0.
v_f = 0: stopping condition W_net = -0.5 m v_0^2.

WEP-04.title: Conservative Forces & Path Independence
WEP-04.definition: A force is conservative if the work it performs along any path depends solely on the initial and final coordinates, which is mathematically equivalent to having zero curl and zero closed-loop line integral.
canonical_rules: Closed path invariant: oint F_c . dr = 0 for any closed contour.
In 2D Cartesian fields F = F_x i + F_y j, conservative condition requires dF_x/dy = dF_y/dx.
Path independence allows selecting the algebraically simplest integration path between two points.
operational_heuristics: Test partial derivative cross-symmetry: dF_x/dy == dF_y/dx.
If symmetric, compute work by path-independent potential difference: W = U(A) - U(B).
boundary_conditions: Closed loop: W_closed = 0.
Friction / drag: oint f . dr < 0 (strictly non-conservative).

WEP-05.title: Gravitational & Elastic Potential Energy Wells
WEP-05.definition: Potential energy U represents stored energy of configuration defined exclusively for conservative interactions via Delta U = -W_c.
canonical_rules: Gravitational potential energy near Earth surface: U_g = m g h (relative to chosen datum h = 0).
Ideal spring elastic potential energy: U_s = 0.5 k x^2 (where x is extension/compression from unstretched equilibrium).
Datum choice is an arbitrary gauge convention; only potential energy differences Delta U have physical significance.
operational_heuristics: Declare datum line U = 0 at the lowest geometric point or relaxed spring position.
Account for both gravitational and elastic components in total potential energy: U = U_g + U_s.
boundary_conditions: x = 0: U_s = 0 (relaxed spring stores zero energy).

WEP-06.title: Conservative Force as Negative Potential Gradient
WEP-06.definition: In conservative fields, the force vector is the negative spatial gradient of the potential energy scalar function: F = -nabla U, or F_x = -dU/dx in 1D.
canonical_rules: Force points in the direction of steepest potential energy descent (downhill on U(x) curve).
Equilibrium points occur where force vanishes: dU/dx = 0.
Stability is determined by the second derivative curvature: d^2U/dx^2 > 0 (stable, local minimum), d^2U/dx^2 < 0 (unstable, local maximum), d^2U/dx^2 = 0 (neutral).
operational_heuristics: Differentiate U(x) to find F(x) = -dU/dx.
Set dU/dx = 0 to locate equilibrium positions.
Evaluate d^2U/dx^2 to classify stability.
boundary_conditions: dU/dx = 0 and d^2U/dx^2 > 0: stable equilibrium (potential trough).
dU/dx = 0 and d^2U/dx^2 < 0: unstable equilibrium (potential crest).

WEP-07.title: Mechanical Energy Conservation & Turning Points
WEP-07.definition: In systems with only conservative forces acting, total mechanical energy E = K + U remains constant. Motion is constrained to regions where E >= U(x), with turning points located where E = U(x) (K = 0).
canonical_rules: Energy conservation equation: 0.5 m v_1^2 + U(x_1) = 0.5 m v_2^2 + U(x_2).
Classical turning points occur where kinetic energy drops to zero: v = 0 => U(x) = E.
In vertical circular loops, maintaining string tension at top requires v_top >= sqrt(g L), leading to critical release velocity v_bot = sqrt(5 g L).
operational_heuristics: Write total energy E = K + U at the initial reference state.
Set K = 0 to find spatial boundaries / turning points of motion.
Combine energy conservation with centripetal force balance (Sigma F_radial = m v^2 / R) for curved paths.
boundary_conditions: E < U_min: classically forbidden region.
Top of vertical circle: T_top = m v_top^2 / L - m g >= 0 => v_top >= sqrt(g L).

WEP-08.title: Power as Rate of Energy Transfer & Drag Scaling
WEP-08.definition: Power is the rate at which work is done or energy is transformed: P = dW/dt = F . v. When resisting drag forces proportional to speed squared (F_drag = k v^2), power required scales with the cube of speed: P = k v^3.
canonical_rules: Instantaneous power: P = F v cos theta.
Average power: P_avg = Total Work / Total Time = Delta W / Delta t.
Constant engine power delivery yields accelerating speed v(t) = sqrt(2 P t / m) and distance x(t) = (2/3) sqrt(2 P / m) t^(3/2).
operational_heuristics: For vehicle cruising at constant velocity: driving force F_engine = sum of resistive forces.
Multiply total resistive force by cruising velocity to find required engine power.
Apply cubic scaling law (P_2 / P_1 = (v_2 / v_1)^3) for aerodynamic cruise regimes.
boundary_conditions: v = 0: instantaneous mechanical power output is zero (P = 0).
Cruising against quadratic drag: doubling velocity requires an 8-fold increase in horsepower.

WEP-09.title: Non-Holonomic Friction Work in Multi-Body Systems
WEP-09.definition: Kinetic friction performs negative work on relative slip interfaces, converting mechanical energy into heat, but can perform positive work on an individual body in a specific reference frame.
canonical_rules: Total interface dissipation: Delta E_thermal = f_k * s_relative >= 0.
In the ground frame, kinetic friction accelerates a box placed on a moving belt, doing positive work W_box = +0.5 m v^2 on the box.
Motor work on the belt is W_motor = f_k s_belt = m v^2, with exactly 50% going to box kinetic energy and 50% dissipated as interface heat.
operational_heuristics: Compute relative slip distance between contacting surfaces: s_rel = s_belt - s_box.
Calculate thermal loss directly: Q_diss = f_k * s_rel.
Balance the energy ledger across both bodies and driving motor.
boundary_conditions: Zero slip (s_rel = 0): static friction performs zero net interface dissipation.
Frictionless belt (mu_k = 0): zero work done, box remains stationary in ground frame.

WEP-10.title: Momentum vs Kinetic Energy Scaling Relations
WEP-10.definition: Momentum p = m v is linear in velocity, whereas kinetic energy K = 0.5 m v^2 = p^2 / (2 m) is quadratic, governing asymmetric energy partitioning between colliding or recoiling bodies.
canonical_rules: Direct relation: K = p^2 / (2m) and p = sqrt(2 m K).
For two bodies possessing equal momentum (p_1 = p_2), kinetic energies scale inversely with mass: K_1 / K_2 = m_2 / m_1.
In explosive or gun recoil events, the lighter body absorbs the overwhelming fraction of total released kinetic energy.
operational_heuristics: Express energy in terms of momentum: substitute K = p^2 / (2m).
For percentage changes: if p increases by x%, K_new / K_old = (1 + x/100)^2.
If mass ratio is m_bullet / M_rifle << 1, bullet carries > 99% of explosion energy.
boundary_conditions: m -> infinity: K -> 0 for finite momentum (immovable barrier absorbs momentum without energy).
Equal kinetic energy: p_1 / p_2 = sqrt(m_1 / m_2).

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: Because centripetal force is large and sustains circular motion, it must perform positive work on the revolving object.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Centripetal force is strictly orthogonal to instantaneous velocity (F_c perp v). Since cos(90 deg) = 0, instantaneous power dW/dt = F . v = 0, and kinetic energy remains strictly invariant.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: A satellite in a circular orbit revolves for billions of years under continuous gravitational pull without any change in orbital speed.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: An object at height h possesses an intrinsic, absolute potential energy mgh regardless of the coordinate system chosen.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Potential energy has physical meaning only through differences Delta U = -W_c. The datum U = 0 is an arbitrary coordinate gauge convention; physics is invariant under any constant shift U -> U + C.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: A book dropped from a desk to the floor acquires the identical Delta K regardless of whether datum is the desk, the floor, or the center of the Earth.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: A higher-power machine always performs more total work than a lower-power machine.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Power is the temporal rate of energy transfer (P = dW/dt). A 1000 W engine running for 2 seconds does 2000 J; a 100 W motor running for 1 hour does 360,000 J. Work is total transferred energy; power is rate.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Comparing a 1000 W dragster engine revved for 2 seconds (2000 J) versus a 200 W cyclist pedaling for 1 hour (720,000 J).

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: Work to stretch a spring by displacement x is force times distance: W = (kx) * x = kx^2.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Spring force increases linearly from 0 to kx. The work is the triangular integral area under Hooke's line: W = int_0^x kx' dx' = 0.5 k x^2 (exactly half the bounding rectangle).
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Integrating force sensor output during spring elongation demonstrates that average resisting force is exactly 0.5 kx, yielding W = 0.5 k x^2.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: Friction always performs negative work on every object it touches.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Kinetic friction performs positive work on a secondary object that is accelerated forward by it (e.g. box placed on moving conveyor belt). Only the net sum across both interacting surfaces is non-positive.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Placing a stationary box on a moving conveyor belt: kinetic friction accelerates the box from rest to belt speed, performing positive work Delta K = +0.5 m v^2 on the box.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.concept: Equal Momentum Implies Equal Energy Fallacy
cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: Two bodies with equal momentum must have identical kinetic energy.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: K = p^2 / (2m). For equal momentum, kinetic energy is inversely proportional to mass. The lighter body moves much faster and carries vastly greater kinetic energy.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Firing a rifle: bullet and rifle have equal and opposite momentum (p_bullet = -p_rifle), yet the light bullet carries > 99% of the powder's kinetic energy.

first_move_atlas.cue: Constant force acting on moving body at an angle
first_move_atlas.representation: Vector dot product diagram with force vector and displacement vector separated by angle theta
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Identify angle theta between F and s; calculate W = F s cos theta; check if theta = 90 deg
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Multiplying total force magnitude by distance without taking the cosine of the angle

first_move_atlas.cue: Position-dependent force F(x) or spring stretch
first_move_atlas.representation: F vs x coordinate graph showing signed area under the force curve
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Set up definite integral W = int_{x_i}^{x_f} F(x) dx or compute geometric triangular/trapezoidal area
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Multiplying final force F(x_f) by total displacement x as if force were constant

first_move_atlas.cue: Speed change under applied forces without time given
first_move_atlas.representation: Work-Energy balance ledger showing W_net = Delta K
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Sum work done by all individual forces and equate to 0.5 m v_f^2 - 0.5 m v_i^2
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Attempting time-dependent kinematics (v = u + at) when acceleration is non-uniform

first_move_atlas.cue: 2D force field given as F(x, y) = F_x i + F_y j
first_move_atlas.representation: Curl check and closed-loop line integral path comparison
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Compute partial derivatives dF_x/dy and dF_y/dx to test if field is conservative
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Assuming any path gives different work without verifying curl first

first_move_atlas.representation: Energy level datum diagram declaring U = 0 reference position
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Declare datum line at lowest point; write U_g = mgh and U_s = 0.5 k x^2
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Confusing spring displacement from equilibrium with vertical height coordinate

first_move_atlas.cue: Potential energy function U(x) given as algebraic formula
first_move_atlas.representation: Potential energy landscape curve U(x) with slope tangents
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Differentiate U(x) to obtain F(x) = -dU/dx; set dU/dx = 0 to find equilibrium positions
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Equating force directly to U(x) or forgetting the essential leading negative sign in F = -dU/dx

first_move_atlas.cue: Conservative motion with turning points or circular loop
first_move_atlas.representation: Total mechanical energy horizontal line E intersecting U(x) curve
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Write E = K + U = const; set K = 0 to find turning points where E = U(x)
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Allowing motion in classically forbidden regions where E < U(x)

first_move_atlas.cue: Engine power, hoist motor, or aerodynamic vehicle drag
first_move_atlas.representation: Power-velocity diagram showing P = F . v and quadratic/cubic curves
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Equate driving force to total resistive force; compute power as P = F_drive * v
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Using P = W / t when velocity or force varies continuously with time

first_move_atlas.cue: Box placed on moving belt or multi-body sliding contact
first_move_atlas.representation: Two-body interface slip diagram showing ground vs belt displacements
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Calculate relative displacement s_rel; compute thermal dissipation as Q = f_k * s_rel
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Assuming kinetic friction does negative work on every body in all reference frames

first_move_atlas.cue: Comparison of kinetic energy and momentum for different masses
first_move_atlas.representation: K vs p parabolic scaling graph: K = p^2 / (2m)
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Use K = p^2 / (2m); for constant momentum, set ratio K_1 / K_2 = m_2 / m_1
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Assuming equal momentum implies equal velocities or equal kinetic energies
